newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 17.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI
--Germany officials claimed yesterday that Intracom boss Socrates Kokkalis collaborated with former East German secret police STASI to further business goals.
--The National Bank will distribute shares to staff, rather than pay increases, as productivity incentives, sources say.
--State-run hospitals are to get private sector management, following yesterday's meeting at the national economy ministry on health spending.
--The General Confederation of Workers of Greece has called a nationwide strike for next Tuesday - the day the new tax bill is submitted to Parliament.
IMERISIA
--The hard drachma is giving rise to new investment products (exotic options), destined for investment portfolios of over one billions drachmas.

--The government is most likely to call for new bids for the Bank of Crete by the summer. Sources say the Bank of Piraeus withdraw its sole offer yesterday. Meanwhile, a number of private banks have shown interest in a sale of the Macedonia-Thrace Bank.
KERDOS
--The Athens Stock Exchange yesterday gave the green light for an increase in share capitals for Euromedica and Ergobank.
--1997 will be a year of expansion and consolidation for the Macedonia-Thrace Bank.
EXPRESS

--The alarm bells start ringing on the fuel market as company, retailers and ministry attempt to work out a solution. The European Commission said it would take Greece to court over not deregulating the market.
--Environment, Town Planning and Public Works Minister Costas Laliotis will chair a meeting today with the Athens Metro company, part of continuing efforts to resolve differences.
--Seamen and dockworkers announced a further 48-hour of strike yesterday, extending the current strike, in its fifth day.
NAFTEMBORIKI

--The finance ministry is planning on introducing benchmarks - a system of multiple issues of bonds - to connect the primary and secondary title markets and reduce the cost of public borrowing as well as creating base interest rates for the market.
--The consumer charge on fuel will fall as of the end of February.
--Development Minister Vasso Papandreou says she may include frnachising in a new development law to be drafted. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
